Twenty-two comments

Skidoo

Stephen Cooney wrote this tune, played by Sharon Shannon on her self-titled cd. They do it in F#minor, but Em is a more fiddle friendly key.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on November 4th, 2001.

Barra MacNeils

The Barra MacNeils also play it in F#minor as part of a set…A great piece.

↳ Posted by Winnowill on November 28th, 2003.

i like the version done by seamus o’sullivan and gerry conlon, great to dance to.

↳ Posted by Champ_irish_dancer on September 3rd, 2006.

This reel is very aptly named: It’s full of adrenaline and attitude, sudden changes of direction…
It is one of the first ‘modern’ Irish tunes I’ve heard. As such it stood out for quite some time before the flood of ‘new generation’ tunes broke the lilting gait…
Do yo know when it was written?

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on November 22nd, 2010.

Skidoo, X:6

Sorry but I don’t find F#m (instead of Amaj) in the list of keys. Any solution?
I directly transcribed it from the playing of Sharon Shannon in F#m (the first time she play it) in https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t_OC5CNRqbY (the link is already given above by NfldWhistler ).
Directly it is not the most confortable on the fiddle, but if you translate it down by one tone, this setting become quite easy to bow when in Em.

↳ Posted by velay-b on November 23rd, 2023.

Skidoo, X:7

The version #6 directly transcribed from Sharon Shannon, but transposed in Em instead of F#m, with a special Hello for fiddlers.

↳ Posted by velay-b on November 23rd, 2023.
